item.title: US Social Security benefits to rise by 3.6 percent in 2027
item.description:
Data: Social Security Administration; Chart: Neil Irwin/Axios Social Security recipients will see the largest rise in their monthly payments in four years in January, with a 3.6% cost-of-living adjustment. Driving the news: The Social Security Administration announced the 2027 COLA adjustment for 76 million recipients of retirement and disability benefits, which by law is calculated based on the Consumer Price Index for the July-through-September quarter. That will increase the average retiree's benefits by $900 a year, or $75 a month. The agency also said that the cutoff for Social Security taxes will rise to $192,300 in 2027, from $184,500 this year. Income above that threshold is not subject to payroll tax. How it works: The adjustment is, by statute, determined by the year-over-year change in CPI for the third quarter. Thus, the September data released this morning was the final…

item.title: Saudi national charged with planting a listening device at OpenAI offices
item.description:
AI agents, meet double agents. OpenAI said it identified, fired, and reported to the FBI an employee who bugged its office. The employee, a Saudi national later identified by law enforcement as Abdulrahman Alfozan, was arrested last week and charged with illegally recording company communication. (He appears to have some ties to members of the Saudi business elite.) Among the evidence against him: chatbot logs about how to install recording devices. Startup espionage has been pursued for far less (see: the Deel-Rippling drama over corporate HR software), but the FBI’s quick work and public rollout of the arrest shows how high the stakes are for the US government and frontier labs. The arrest comes days before the White House AI task force’s first meeting . Its chair, Jay Clayton, cited the case as proof the group is needed. — Rohan Goswami

Early-stage deals have thinned out, which leaves fewer companies ready for growth rounds in 2027. Data: Bureau of Labor Statistics ; Chart: Courtenay Brown/Axios U.S. inflation picked up in September as soaring energy prices added to already stubborn price pressures, the Labor Department said on Wednesday. Why it matters: The latest Consumer Price Index shows that the inflation fight is far from over — and makes further Federal Reserve interest rate hikes more likely as Americans struggle with higher costs. By the numbers: CPI rose 0.6% in September from the prior month, with the annual inflation rate at 3.7%, the government said. That compares with a 0.4% monthly increase and a 3.4% annual rate in August. Core prices, which exclude volatile food and energy costs, gained 0.3% on the month, compared with a similar monthly gain in August. item.title: A bear with a taste for honey: Winnie the Pooh turns 100
item.description:
Winnie-the-Pooh turns 100 today. Actually, that’s not quite true. Yes, A.A. Milne’s beloved book Winnie-the-Pooh , with equally beloved illustrations by E.H. Shepard, was first published on October 14, 1926. But the eponymous bear first appeared by name in a short story—illustrated by J.H. Dowd rather than Shepard—that Milne then expanded into the first chapter of what quickly became and has remained a classic of children’s literature. That story, “The Wrong Sort of Bees,” came out in London’s Evening News on Christmas Eve 1925; the previous year, Milne had written a poem for Punch that features Edward Bear, who, even in a brief appearance, is recognizably Winnie-the-Pooh’s prototype. And perhaps Winnie-the-Pooh would never have had a birthday at all had a very young Christopher Robin Milne not received a stuffed bear from Harrods from his mother in 1921, only a little over a decade…
